Sunlight contains all colors of the visible spectrum, and as it passes through Earth's atmosphere, gas molecules scatter the shorter-wavelength blue and violet light much more strongly than longer-wavelength red and yellow light (a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering). Although violet light is scattered even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue and the upper atmosphere absorbs some violet, so the sky appears predominantly blue to us.
